chapter: Dance and brass bands of Alice's youth
title: Alice on jazz heard on records versus reading music in her day
summary: Alice has only heard George's band on records, says earlier bands read music, and notes the term 'ragtime' wasn't used in her time.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: I was wondering about the first kind of music, something like George, you've heard George's band. I guess you don't get around to hear it very much, but you've heard his records. That type of music.
I never have the chance of going where George is playing with the whole band. She just heard the records. I'm wondering when you... Just the records, that's all I heard.
When you were young, did you ever hear any music, something like that, that type of music? No. Like George plays note.
No. It was, they play with music, you see, the note. They used to have read it off of the music. Yes, but now they play by routines. That's what they call jazz, eh? Yes.
Did they ever use the word writing time? In my days, no.
But when did that word come in?
I don't know when that come in, but in my days they didn't have that right time.
I see. Probably, maybe they had to change the syndrome, not beginning.
Do you remember the first time you heard any of the songs? Mm-hm.
